events.title: Cornwallis Surrenders at Yorktown
events.description: British General Charles Cornwallis surrendered his army of roughly 8,000 men to American and French forces under George Washington and the Comte de Rochambeau after a siege at Yorktown, Virginia.
events.significance: The surrender effectively ended major combat in the American Revolutionary War and led to British recognition of American independence in the 1783 Treaty of Paris.

events.title: Napoleon Begins Retreat from Moscow
events.description: After occupying Moscow for about five weeks without securing a Russian surrender, Napoleon's Grande Armée began its withdrawal from the city as winter approached and supplies dwindled.
events.significance: The disastrous retreat destroyed most of the Grande Armée and marked a turning point in the Napoleonic Wars, weakening French dominance in Europe.

events.title: Black Monday Stock Market Crash
events.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 508 points, or about 22.6 percent, in a single day, the largest one-day percentage drop in its history, with markets worldwide also plunging.
events.significance: The crash prompted reforms such as trading curbs known as circuit breakers and showed how interconnected and automated global financial markets had become.

events.title: Death of King John of England
events.description: King John died of dysentery at Newark Castle during the First Barons' War, leaving the throne to his nine-year-old son, Henry III.
events.significance: His death eased the baronial rebellion and led to reissues of Magna Carta, which helped establish the principle that the monarch was subject to law.

events.title: Marriage of Ferdinand and Isabella
events.description: Ferdinand of Aragon and Isabella of Castile married in Valladolid, joining two of the most powerful Iberian kingdoms in a dynastic union.
events.significance: The union laid the foundation for the unified Spain, which later sponsored Columbus's voyages and became a major global empire.
